evidence: Calculation on idealised aggregates (equal randomly oriented plates joined by single contacts from hierarchical ballistic cluster-cluster aggregation) with geometric drag-sharing rules; no measured junction strength, flow field or lunar breakup. The Earth calibration assumes 4-6 cm flakes sit at their breaking point.
reading_rule: Loads are in units of the plate weight m0 g (force) and m0 g d0 (moment); normalised loads are F/(m g) and M/(m g D) with m the aggregate mass and D its maximum dimension. "shadow" gives each pixel of projected area to the lowest plate (opaque, the upper bound on uneven drag), "own" to every plate over it (no shadowing, the lower bound), "partial" in shares 0.5^rank. Ratios are lunar over Earth span at equal peak junction load; spans come from power-law fits over sizes from N plates up, N named in each key (from64, from256).
assumptions: The aggregates are equal plates joined by single contacts, so the contacts form a tree; natural flakes interlock and share a moment over several contacts.

The aggregates grow by joining equal clusters; natural flakes grow largely by sweeping much smaller crystals and flakes, a history that changes the contact tree and may move the largest remnant share.
The aggregates are sparser in projection than natural flakes (area ratio 0.08-0.14 against 0.35), which weakens their shadowing; the dense limit, moments in proportion to m g D, brackets that side.

Drag is shared by geometric rules at flake Reynolds numbers of 3000-6700; wakes, flow through the porous flake and edge effects are not resolved. The orientation is fixed and the loads are instantaneous.
Every junction is equally strong at every flake size, and Earth flakes of 4-6 cm sit at their breaking point; only the first failure is followed.
